summary: Headings (h1 to h6) give a page its outline, and p holds a paragraph of text. Browsers and screen readers use the heading levels to understand how the page is organized.
notes: Use one <h1> for the page title, then <h2> for each section. Do not skip levels (h2 straight to h4).

Each

is its own paragraph. Pressing Enter in your code does not make a new paragraph on screen; a new

does.
<strong> and <em> add meaning (important, stressed). The bold and italic look comes from the browser's default styles.
pitfall: Picking <h4> because it looks the right size. The heading level describes structure; change the size in CSS instead.
